suggestions: No look-ahead in the forecast (rule 3 in spirit; A1 already applies it to reports). A forecast analog could be a history track that started before tonight but was still flying at `q.until`, for example a same-night flight at the same installation. Its recovery point and remainder would then come from the future. Mirror A1's `report_ts_ms <= until` line: treat a recovery point as known only when the analog's `end_ts <= q.until`. Cover it in `test_forecast_and_recall_ignore_points_after_t` or a sibling test.

A7 makes `live_rank1_report_for` require DELTA among the top 3 matched incidents at T+120. D-081 shows DELTA at #1 at T+90, but no planning fact measures its rank at T+120 with the shipped model. Measure it early in the build. Fact 2 is also an aggregate, so confirm that the planted report is the only report (or the top-ranked one) inside P1-DELTA-260419's filter window. D-011 only guarantees that the incident has a lone report.

Rule 6 (ports): A3's `check_reports_index` relies on a row count from `LanceReportIndex.count`, which is not on the `ReportIndex` Protocol. Either add `count` to `ports.py` and log it in D-085, or state that this guard sits at adapter level under D-053. Recall and eval business logic should not call a LanceDB-only method.

`test_delta_report_is_rank1_for_the_delta_match` runs on toy models. To keep it stable, call `ReportRecall.for_match` on the DELTA candidate directly. Do not depend on DELTA appearing among the toy model's matches; the real-model claim already lives in the slow test and the eval demo row.

CLAUDE.md's library notes say `tbl.create_fts_index("text")`. The plan uses `create_index("text", config=FTS(with_position=True))` because the former is deprecated and phrase queries need positions. Record this deviation explicitly in D-085, as CLAUDE.md asks when the installed version behaves differently.

A9 says it is registered before any build measurement, but planning fact 5 already computed the training-split numbers (311 m against 502 m). D-090 should say plainly that the outcome of its rule was known at registration time, not only that eval-split numbers were seen.

The margin on `forecast_median_t90_m` is thin: 384 m as written on the eval queries. If `match_kind` is adopted, report both modes' eval-split medians in REPORT.md so the gate result can be read in context.

Consider building `extract_clues` on `sim.lexicon` (the `VEHICLES` tuple, or the colour-required part of `_VEHICLE_RE`) so recall and the generator share one vocabulary. The existing `test_reports_every_clue_has_a_truth_row` already shows reports never use bare vehicle types.

R9: a run-to-run latency change of more than 5% could trip `make eval`'s baseline-regression exit. The plan keeps downstream work outside the timed span, which is right; confirm in EXIT_CHECK.md that the latency keys did not move.
summary: The plan covers all four Phase 5 task checkboxes: the hashing and FastEmbed embedders with `fetch-models`; the LanceDB `reports` table with FTS, hybrid search with filters and the RRF fallback; clue extraction, `report_clues` and linking across matches and to the forecast zone; and `forecast/analog.py` with the `recall` and `forecast` commands. Every SPEC test bullet has a named test: determinism and L2 norm, exact-phrase FTS, the base and time filters, DELTA rank 1 (fast, slow and eval demo row), the ≤ 400 m demo forecast (slow test and demo row) and County Rd 12 crossing the zone. The exit-check table maps `make index`, `make eval`, the `forecast` command and `scripts/check_targets.py 5` to concrete evidence. The metric and demo keys match those `check_targets.py` reads (`report_linkage`, `forecast_median_t90_m`, `live_rank1_report_for`, `forecast_error_max_m`). Spot checks against the repo hold up: the `ReportIndex` port, `stable_int`, `geo.rotate`, `dtw_rerank.warp_path`, the lexicon constants, the current `STUBS`, D-082 as the next free decision number, and the generator emitting only coloured vehicle clues. The rules are respected. Truth reads stay in `eval/` and tests. Recall filters on `event_ts < q.start` and `report_ts <= until`. The hashing embedder is the offline default, with no runtime downloads. The anchor choice is decided by a training-split rule registered in advance, so no human decision is needed. One blocking issue: the documentation list omits `src/kairos_defense/README.md`, which still describes `recall`, `forecast` and `fetch-models` as stubs and would go stale, against CLAUDE.md's current-README rule. It is a one-line fix. The suggestions cover a possible look-ahead in forecast analogs, an unmeasured DELTA rank at T+120, and port purity of the reports-index guard.
